clue.text: Time of year to secure time in office? Not quite

parts.note: to secure something is to win it

indicators.note: not quite says the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: a term is a spell of office, such as a president's

explanation.surface: A politician hoping to clinch a period in office but falling just short.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark and 'Not quite' read as political doubt; 'Not quite' actually docks the last letter of TERM, leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: It is one of the four seasons, the coldest part of the calendar.

clue.text: Promise to support development of what will enshrine Conservative slogan

indicators.note: to support in a down clue places this piece below the rest
will enshrine means the rearranged letters hold the abbreviation within
development of says the word's letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
a word is a promise, as in giving your word

explanation.surface: A Conservative pledge to back policy, framed as a campaign slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'development of' is the anagram signal, giving WATCH once C is enshrined; 'to support' works because in a down clue the lower piece holds up the upper one.
explanation.definitionFit: A rallying cry or motto expressing a group's principles is a synonym for slogan.

clue.text: Germany supporting uprising in African country

indicators.note: supporting in a down clue puts this piece underneath
uprising in a down clue means the little word reads upwards

explanation.surface: German backing for a rebellion in an African state.
explanation.definitionFit: This West African nation is landlocked and named after its great river.

clue.text: One's first in library, possibly securing edition? On the contrary

indicators.note: securing would put one piece round the other
On the contrary flips the stated roles, so the edition holds the shuffled letters
possibly says the word's letters could be rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone first into the library, hunting for a particular edition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' reverses the roles that 'securing' states: the edition does the securing, not the anagram of 'library'.
explanation.definitionFit: An early riser or prompt arriver is the one who gets there ahead of everyone.

clue.text: Trip negotiated corners, avoiding borders, in great pleasure

indicators.note: in places the trimmed word inside the other

parts.note: joy is great pleasure

indicators.note: avoiding borders means the word loses its outer letters at each end

parts.note: a vehicle that negotiated corners turned

explanation.surface: A driver delighting in a trip round winding roads, keeping off the verges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding borders' takes the end letters off the synonym, not off the clue words, leaving URNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A trip is a journey from one place to another; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: I will need place to rest after Judge scoffed

indicators.note: after puts the other pieces behind the judge's letter

parts.note: a bed is a place to rest

explanation.surface: Someone mocked by a judge and told they need a lie-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To jeer or mock someone, past tense; scoffed in the sense of sneered.

clue.text: Characters participating in round of Open

indicators.note: characters means letters, and participating in says they are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Golfers taking part in a round of the Open championship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Open' looks like the golf tournament but is a verb: to unfasten.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a knot or a button is to unfasten it, to open it.

clue.text: Child-minder to attack farm animal

parts.note: a nanny looks after children
to go at someone is to attack them

explanation.surface: A babysitter set upon by livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the female of a horned farmyard animal kept for milk.

clue.text: Conference venue at place that's elevated

indicators.note: that's elevated in a down clue means the letters read upwards

parts.note: to lay something is to place it

explanation.surface: A conference held somewhere on high ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Both words go upwards together: AT LAY reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1945 meeting of Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin took place in this Crimean resort.

clue.text: Nothing in promotional material he had turned up

indicators.note: in puts the zero inside the publicity word

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity
O is zero, nothing
he'd is the contraction of he had

explanation.surface: A man's advertising leaflets ending up empty, or appearing out of nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' looks like 'appeared', but means soil turned over by a farmer.
explanation.definitionFit: Earth that a farmer has broken and turned over with a blade has been tilled.

clue.text: Row about good contender taking things seriously?

indicators.note: about means the first word goes round the letter

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats

explanation.surface: A dispute over whether a decent rival is being earnest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a line of seats. The definition is playful: a fierce, determined competitor is called a tiger.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is slang for a fiercely committed competitor, one who fights hard for every point.

clue.text: Lusty librarian getting laid possibly, keeping at home

parts.note: lib. is a dictionary abbreviation for librarian

indicators.note: keeping says the reshuffled letters hold the other piece within them
possibly says these letters could be arranged another way

parts.note: at home means in

explanation.surface: A racy picture of a librarian enjoying a romantic encounter at home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' is the anagram signal, making IDAL; lib. for librarian is a dictionary abbreviation rarely seen outside crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Lusty here means full of sexual desire, the libido being the sex drive.

clue.text: Instrument picked up on the radio — unknown chap hogging most odd bits of radio

indicators.note: on the radio says the word is as listeners would hear it spoken

parts.note: to have picked up a sound is to have heard it
Y is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: hogging means the outer piece keeps the letters within itself

parts.note: a guy is a chap

indicators.note: most means all but the last of those letters
odd bits of means the first, third and fifth letters

explanation.surface: A wandering musician's instrument heard on air, with a stranger taking up the airtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd bits of' gives three letters and 'most' drops the last, the O. The sound-alike only works in a non-rhotic accent, where the R is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a medieval stringed instrument played by turning a crank, a rosined wheel bowing the strings.

clue.text: Talkative bird belonging to the writer recalled article

parts.note: the setter's possessive is my

indicators.note: recalled means the little word is read backwards

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A writer remembering a piece about their own chattering pet bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This Asian starling is famous for mimicking human speech, as a parrot does.

clue.text: Not trendy? Trendy? Just tell me!

parts.note: something unfashionable is said to be out
a fashionable person is with it

explanation.surface: An exasperated exchange about whether something is fashionable, ending in a demand for a straight answer.
explanation.walkthrough: The two opposites sit side by side, and the third part is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an impatient command to speak up and reveal something at once.

clue.text: Beat no longer, reaching edge of consciousness

parts.note: to thresh is to beat, as grain
something old is no longer current

explanation.surface: A pulse fading as someone slips toward awareness.
explanation.definitionFit: In psychology the limit below which a stimulus is not perceived is called the limen.

clue.text: Attempt to grab a waistcoat in America? It's a farce

indicators.note: to grab means the outer word clutches the others inside

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Americans call a waistcoat a vest

explanation.surface: A bungled snatch of an American waistcoat, a complete farce.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is an undershirt; the US sense is the sleeveless garment worn under a jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: An absurd or grotesque mockery of something is a farce, a sham.

clue.text: Line in meals, perhaps, offering excessive supply

indicators.note: in puts the letter inside the other word

parts.note: meals are an example of food

explanation.surface: A caterer's queue for meals offering more than enough to go round.
explanation.definitionFit: A deluge or glut of something, such as letters, is an overwhelming surplus.

clue.text: Daring swimmer, note, circling water plant

indicators.note: circling means the banknote word goes round the plant

parts.note: a fiver is a British five-pound note
a reed grows in water

explanation.surface: A bold swimmer and a music note round a pond plant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks musical but is a banknote: a fiver is a five-pound note.
explanation.definitionFit: This is someone who descends underwater on one breath without breathing apparatus, a risky sport.

clue.text: Trick Duke: Queen not attending formal function

indicators.note: not attending means the letter is absent from the word

parts.note: a reception is a formal gathering
R, for regina, means queen

explanation.surface: A duke deceived because the Queen skipped a state occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruse or ploy that misleads is a synonym; both nouns mean fooling someone.

clue.text: Challenged about blocking father

indicators.note: blocking means the little word sits in the middle of the other and obstructs it

parts.note: dad means father
re means about, as in a memo heading

explanation.surface: Someone defied after getting in their father's way.
explanation.definitionFit: Challenged someone to do something risky: the two verbs are synonyms in the past tense.

clue.text: Face heading off frantic debate?

parts.note: dial is slang for face

indicators.note: heading off says the word loses its first letter

parts.note: hectic means frantic

explanation.surface: A frenzied argument where someone storms off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Face' is the old slang 'dial' for a face; the question mark flags that debate is an example of the method.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectic is the art of reasoning through argument and counter-argument, so a debate is one instance.

clue.text: Staff comment on website?

definitions.meaning: a staff is a pole or stake, an upright support
a message left on an online forum or blog

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an upright stake and a message placed on an internet board.

clue.text: Prince about to get on alert system?

indicators.note: about means the prince's letters go round the other word

parts.note: to get on in years is to age

explanation.surface: A prince nearing old age gets an alarm system.
explanation.definitionFit: A bleeper alerts doctors and others to calls; the question mark marks it as a kind of alerting device.

clue.text: What China offers last boat after end of week at work

indicators.note: after puts the two words following the day's abbreviation

parts.note: Friday, abbreviated Fri, ends the working week
the last of something is its end
a boat is a ship

explanation.surface: A Friday-afternoon final ferry, like a nation's goodwill gesture.
explanation.walkthrough: China is rhyming slang: 'china plate' means mate, a friend in Britain. The capital C helps hide it.
explanation.definitionFit: A mate offers companionship, the bond between pals.

clue.text: Just clever to abandon Britain

indicators.note: to abandon means the letter leaves the word

parts.note: bright means clever

explanation.surface: A smart person justly deciding to leave the country.
explanation.definitionFit: Just as an adjective means fair, morally correct.

clue.text: A measure of the frequency injuries featured on the radio

indicators.note: featured on the radio says the word is as it would be broadcast and heard

parts.note: hurts are injuries

explanation.surface: A tally of how often injuries come up in sports broadcasts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frequency' seems to mean how often; it is the physics sense, measured in cycles per second.
explanation.definitionFit: The SI unit of cycles per second, used for radio wavelengths, sound pitch and more.

clue.text: Almost due to get data

indicators.note: almost means the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: to be in for something is to be due it

explanation.surface: A deadline approaching for handing over figures.
explanation.walkthrough: 'due' gives the two-word phrase IN FOR, as in 'in for a surprise'.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a casual shortening of information, facts and figures.

clue.text: Daughter close to tears initially after sentimental stuff in farewell

indicators.note: after puts the daughter and following pieces behind the sentimental stuff

parts.note: goo is sickly sentimentality
nigh means close or near

indicators.note: initially means the word supplies only its first letter

explanation.surface: A daughter on the verge of tears in a mushy bedtime parting.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a parting word said at night, a form of saying goodbye.

clue.text: Composer contributing to squalid revue after reflection

indicators.note: after reflection says the hidden letters are read backwards
contributing to says the letters are part of the words that follow, lying within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A composer offering music to a seedy stage show and having second thoughts.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Composer contributing' as the definition, leaving the hidden step with no indicator; 'contributing to' is that indicator, so the definition is just 'Composer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Giuseppe Verdi was the Italian who wrote the operas Aida and La Traviata.

clue.text: Engineers a little taken aback about company soldier, as before

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers

indicators.note: about says the reversed word goes round the other piece
taken aback means the word is turned round

parts.note: a tad is a little

explanation.surface: Army engineers slightly startled by a historical soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken aback' makes DAT, read as surprise in the surface. 'as before' marks the definition as historical.
explanation.definitionFit: British infantrymen of earlier centuries wore scarlet tunics, hence this name for them.

clue.text: Disney film sees Australian following river into morass

indicators.note: into places the pair inside the marsh word

parts.note: a fen is marshy ground, a morass

indicators.note: following puts the Australian after the river

parts.note: Oz is slang for Australia or Australian

explanation.surface: An Australian adventurer tracking a river into a swamp, like a cartoon plot.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the 2013 animated musical about sisters Elsa and Anna.
